blogs.title: 🚀 The story behind “Drone 2”: My KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 keynote
blogs.content: Posted on November 25, 2026 by Lin Sun (CNCF Ambassador and KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Co-Chair) CNCF projects highlighted in this post An open source adventure featuring Kubernetes, agent-substrate, kagent, AI agents, drones, and more! Just 30 seconds before going live for the KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA 2026 closing keynote, “Cloud Native Without Limits: What Can AI Agents Do for Us?”, while Abdel Sghiouar was introducing me, Cory Jett leaned over and whispered: “The drone isn’t connecting to the controller!” 😱 A heart-stopping moment! Thankfully, a quick reboot saved the day. And then came the moment I’ll never forget: walking onto the stage with a live drone following right behind me! 🚁✨ And when I finally walked off stage, all the nervousness and anxiety were gone. I was just SO happy! What a feeling! ❤️ On-stage live demo with the drone and big screens 🥋 From Amsterdam to Salt Lake City: Never give up! After my Amsterdam keynote , where the drone camera failed, Christian Dussol taught me the martial arts lesson of “Osu” (never give up! 🥋💪). That lesson stuck with me, and I wanted to push the boundaries even further in Salt Lake City. Striking the “Osu” posture after the Amsterdam keynote While brainstorming with Allison Price around our theme, “Cloud Native Without Limits,” we asked ourselves: What if we could let the audience experience what it’s like to fly and build something live on stage, powered by AI agents? Of course, bringing a live drone indoors isn’t exactly plug-and-play. There was quite a bit of work behind the scenes! 🛠️ Behind the scenes: Making the impossible possible A few challenges we had to tackle: 🛩️ Regulatory compliance: Back in August, we learned that an FAA Part 107-certified remote pilot was required for our indoor drone operation. Cory stepped up, completed the necessary training in just one week, and saved the demo! 🙌 Teaser at the venue 😅 🏠 Home testing: I got propeller guards so I could safely experiment with code, test flight paths, and practice flying indoors at home. Let’s just say my house became a mini drone testing lab! Flight testing at home with propeller guards But this demo was about much more than flying a drone. We wanted to show what real-time agentic execution looks like, with the right guardrails, sandboxing, and observability in place. 🤖 Under the hood: The Cloud Native technologies behind the drone Here’s what powered the experience: 🤖 Agents: Running on CNCF Sanbox projects agent-substrate , and kagent providing an opinionated layer for building and running agents. 🔐Then AAIF Growth project agentgateway : Playing multiple roles: LLM gateway: Rate limiting and controlling access to models. Egress gateway (as part of agent-substrate): Enforcing sandbox and network access policies. MCP gateway: Handling authentication and authorization for Model Context Protocol tool calls with an Identity Provider, for example, Keycloak. 📊 OpenTelemetry and Jaeger: Providing end-to-end observability across agent execution through agentgateway and agent-substrate, including rate-limiting errors, the duration of each tool call, and where agents spend most of their time. All coming together to make an AI-powered physical experience happen, live on stage! The moment when it all comes together live on stage 💜 A big Thank You & what’s next? 🇪🇸 The community’s response was incredible! It’s exciting to see how far we’ve come as an industry, bringing AI models, agentic AI, and cloud native technologies together to make things possible that would have seemed like science fiction just a few years ago. A massive THANK YOU to my manager, Idit Levine , for her unwavering support; Cory Jett , for making the drone flight possible; Allison Price , for brainstorming this adventure with me; Jonathan Bryce , for loving the drone idea when I casually brought it up during KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA 2025; Elna Vogel , for making sure we had the required insurance. And of course, a huge shout-out to the entire event and technical teams who helped bring this adventure to life! ❤️ Last but definitely not least, THANK YOU to the agent-substrate, kagent, and agentgateway communities! They answered every question I threw at them, responded incredibly quickly, and were always ready to jump in and debug live if needed. I couldn’t have pulled this off without you! 💜 My #substrate-dev team CNCF slack 📺 Missed the keynote? Catch the full recording! Now, I’m officially wrapping up the Drone 2 chapter and already looking forward to building something fresh for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon 2027 in Barcelona! 🇪🇸 So, what physical objects or hardware should we hack on next? Drones have had their moment. What’s next? What could we build that I haven’t even imagined yet? 🙂 Share
